Recently a testing log for SCP-143 was created, so naturally it would make sense for there to be a crosslink between this test log and its base article. The WikiWalk team felt that the log would best be included within the containment procedures instead of the end of the article since 143 already ends on a pretty good note, and we don't want to bork the articles rhythm. As such, recommending the following changes:

Editing this:

It is important that no one be within the containment area when SCP-143 begins to shed.

To read:

It is important that no one be within the containment area when SCP-143 begins to shed, however after the shedding has concluded, the collection of the fallen petals for testing purposes has been authorized by the project director (see SCP-143 Testing Log).

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: Gratuitous Japanese
item.content:encoded:
"jinki no kodachi" (刃木の木立ち), or the "Bladewood Grove."

Okay, this has been bothering me badly. "kodachi" (meaning "grove") is represented in kanji as ”木立”.

If we read the kanji/kana here, it would be "jinki no kodachichi"… which is certainly not "Bladewood Grove".

For the sake of spelling, can we change it to ”刃木の木立”？

item.title: Re: I'm gonna ask what might be a dumb question:
item.content:encoded:
Why do so many people KNOW about these things?

Probably because they've known since before the Foundation got involved in 1905?

would the Foundation not have amnestic-ified this family and sent them off to do something else, after getting all known information about these trees from them?

I dunno if that would benefit the Foundation much. Secrecy is important, yeah, but eliminating the family would require the Foundation to invest time and resources into training replacements, plus smoothing over any objections from the government that would inevitably result from mind-wiping and relocating a traditional family from the property they've held for generations. Besides, the family doesn't exactly advertise what they're doing, and the products stay within Japan. Seems pretty tidy, so far as what the article has stated goes.

(Or maybe they made the family Foundation staff, idk.)

Staff by extension, maybe, but there's no reason to shove the family into Foundation protocol when they're effectively caretakers with no strong ties to the scientific community at large.

So it would seem. Unless an article is kinda blatantly saying something like "zomg titanium is being used because it's kewl", I usually gloss over it being mentioned. When you brought it up there, I did some cursory searching and multiple sources appear to state it has one of the best S2Ws out there.

It really is a pretty interesting metal, so I can see why using it can be so darn tempting, but most things (in a first draft) using it for containment could be kept in a concrete cell or iron lockbox or something, which is why 022-J exists. lol

item.title: (no title)

While it may not be the end-all, be-all of metals, titanium (from some very cursory searching) does apparently have an excellent strength-to-weight ratio, so the comparison seems fitting, imo. S2W can be an important factor in crafting things (which is why planes and stuff use a lot of titanium), so this looks okay to me.

Now, if it had in there that the people gathering the petals were required to wear standard issue titanium exoskeletons, with extra layers of titanium protection underneath… then I'd say yeah, the boner for titanium needs to be dialed back a bit. =P

item.content:encoded: Speaking of which, Prunoideae is the subfamily and Prunus the genus. Binomial names consist of the genus and species, not family and genus. The appropriate Latin name here would be Prunus x yedoensis (for the most common sakura variety; the common name covers several species and a raft of cultivars). Is this just nitpicky, or would you like an edit for that bit of realism?
